description.value: The study examined neural responses during an emotion regulation fMRI task in adolescents with and without histories of suicidal ideation.

spans.text: Here we examine whether SI is associated with neural responses during an emotion regulation fMRI task in a group of adolescents (N=49) ages 13 to 20 years old ( M = 16.95).

SI was considered present ( 1 ) for any of the following: a score greater than zero on the Scale for Suicidal Ideation (SSI; self-report for past two weeks; ( 34 ), a response of “yes” to the SI question on the Diagnostic Interview Schedule for Children Version IV (DISC; past year questions( 35 ), or a response of “yes” to the SI question on the Self-Injurious Thoughts and Behaviors Interview (SITBI; clinical interview covering SI age of onset and age of most recent SI; ( 36 ).
SI was assessed using data from well-validated self-report and structured clinical interviews.

instructions.value: For look trials, participants were instructed to look at the image and allow their emotions to unfold naturally without altering their emotional reaction. For decrease trials, they were instructed to use cognitive reappraisal strategies to reduce their emotional reaction by imagining the scene as psychologically distant, further away, not involving them, or involving actors. After each stimulus, they rated the strength of their emotional reaction on a 5-point Likert scale.
